## - Bitcoin You can donate bitcoin to Voat using their Coinbase page - https://www.coinbase.com/voat

The donate bitcoin link can be found on the sidebar of the front page - https://voat.co

The Coinbase page will provide a different address for each donation, previous bitcoin donations to Voat were done using a static address which for reference you can find below.

Previous static addresses for Voat:

* https://tradeblock.com/bitcoin/address/1BFqer7P9qqqiirbC63KqxfuZYXxk6RrBZ * https://tradeblock.com/bitcoin/address/1C4Q1RvUb3bzk4aaLVgGccnSnaHYFdESzY

----------

If you're new to Bitcoin you can find some links below, take some time to do some research and due diligence. The easiest way to get started is by downloading a wallet to an Android or iOS device (For the best security don't use a jailbroken device). For Android I recommend [Mycelium](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mycelium.wallet) and for iOS I recommend [Breadwallet](http://breadwallet.com).

Both of these wallets use a recovery sentence/back-up phrase (12-24 random words). Write these words down on paper in the order they appear, keep it safe as this will allow you to recover your wallet should something happen to your device.

Once you've set up a wallet you can then buy some bitcoin and send it to your device. Any bitcoin you buy should always be sent to a wallet you have full control of, avoid keeping a balance with any third parties. When you have bitcoins confirmed in your wallet (Wating for at least 6 confirmations will take around 1 hour) you can then send some to Voat.

* [How to use Bitcoin on Android: An easy guide to Mycelium](http://satoshicounter.com/2015/07/09/mycelium/) * [How to use Bitcoin on iPhone: An easy guide to Breadwallet](http://satoshicounter.com/2015/07/14/breadwallet/) * [How to use Bitcoin on Linux / OSX / Windows: An easy guide to Electrum](http://satoshicounter.com/2015/07/14/electrum/) * [HowToBuyBitcoins.info](https://howtobuybitcoins.info) * [How to choose the right Bitcoin exchange](http://bitcoinx.io/bitcoin-help/how-to-choose-the-right-bitcoin-exchange/)

Buying bitcoin is country specific so use the above links to find the best place for your region. [Circle.com](https://www.circle.com) and [Coinbase.com](https://www.coinbase.com) are usually recommend for being easy for beginners to use.

----------

Ensure you don't get all your news and information from just one source or multiple sources all controlled by the same individuals, decentralise all the things.

## - Contribute to the code Voat is open source so you can help fix or improve the sites code on GitHub - https://github.com/voat/voat

Site suggestions and preferences are best made here - http://voat.co/v/ideasforvoat

Site development commentary can go here - http://voat.co/v/voatdev

## - Advertise on Voat You can contact Voat by email through hello@voat.co for all enquiries.

For more information about advertising on Voat visit https://voat.co/advertize

## - Contribute to the discussion New accounts will be limited by what they can do on Voat so get involved and post interesting comments to remove restrictions. You may find it hard to contribute to small or niche subverses but don't be deterred, you should also participate in larger subverses as well as the smaller ones.

## - Browse and voat Subscribe to [subverses](https://voat.co/subverses) you find interesting and then visit https://voat.co/new.

Voat is small so upvoat content you think contributes to the subverse it's posted in, even if you dislike or disagree with it as it will help to keep the small or niche subverses active. Try to only use downvoats for content which doesn't belong in the subverse it's posted in.

If you're feeling adventurous visit https://voat.co/v/all/new and see more content which you might have otherwise missed. Remember if you see a subverse you don't like you can block it which will then make it easier to see other subverses and will stop it from showing up on https://voat.co/v/all.

You could also visit /v/vocatalog which attempts to index subverses by categories and should make it easier to find a topic you're interested in.

## - Help moderators and keep them in check Message the moderators if you see content which doesn't belong such as spam, malware or doxxing but don't report for simply being something you don't agree with.

Remember different subverses will be run differently, subverses which are owned by @system will usually be unmoderated. Some subverses will have loose moderation and some will have strict moderation. It's best to check the subverse's sidebar before posting to see if it has any rules or guidelines. If you have a small display then the sidebar will be visible by pressing the hamburger icon (Three lines on the top left of the page) and then you can scroll the panel which appears.

Also see - https://voat.co/help/faq

Voat has moderator logs for every subverse, I've placed links to these on the sidebars of all the subverses I moderate (Edit: I've removed my own links as Voat now includes these links on the sidebars of all subverses). I will remove all types of spam content but I will not remove peoples views or opinions. If you see something I've removed you don't agree with then let me know, feedback is welcome. I'm here to clean up, not set a narrative.
